main_text.p: unitate. in omnibus autem binis rebus est & consensio & dissensio; consensio per affirmationem unitatis, dissensio vero per negationem ejusdem.

30 Cum Dissentaneorum ratio in dis‑sociatione aut divisione consistat, & eo‑rum unum in sua propria natura non pen‑deat ab altero qua Dissentaneum est, quoad esse, existere, vel sciri, idcirco sunt æqualis luminis & æqualium utrinque virium in arguendo; quapropter etiam uno nomine, unaque definitione per singulas species continentur. quæ omnia longe aliter se habent in consentaneis. in ipsa tamen na‑turali accommodatione qua eorum affe-&tio exercetur, illustrant sese mutuo vi ipsius dissensionis.

3 1 Dissociatio rerum duplici gradu fit: quædam enim ita dissociantur ut possint consociari, quoniam externe tantum dis-sentiunt & sola ratione; vel respectu alicujus argumentalis affectionis, in qua convenire possent ex natura sua: & hæc appellantur diversa, quia quasi divertunt & secedunt paululum à se invicem sine alienatione constante: Quædam autem ita dissociantur, ut non possint consociari vel conjungi, quoniâ interne etiâ dissentiunt, ac reali natura sua, id est, ipsa materia vel forma :

page.notes: Part 1 of 2: the page continues beyond the cut. The right-hand strip shows fragments of the facing page only. Words with doubtful letters: "sciri" and "consentaneis" are printed as shown; the printed form "Dissentaneorum" and "Dissentaneum" are read from the scan with the italic capital D. The first line is partly cut off at the top; "&tio" is read as "ratio"-ending "&tio" (likely "ratio" or "actio") and marked as doubtful. Greek and Latin letters are printed as in the scan.
